doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: One-line impressions of Malcolm X, Ali and others
summary: Quick answers about Malcolm X, Sugar Ray Robinson, Martin Luther King and Muhammad Ali.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Well, three speaks volumes. Three speaks volumes. Let me just run
some names. Just one-line responses. Just names. These are non-music people. Malcolm X.
A man who happened when he should have happened.
He was the Charlie Parker and the John Coltrane of fisticuffs.
He was the John Coltrane and the Charlie Parker of rhetoric and oratory.
That leaves a hell of a gap for this next one. Muhammed Ali.
[Laughs]. He was the greatest because he believed he was the greatest.
